description: Geometry regression tests. The model must be rebuilt from the current control document, must close its own arithmetic identities, and must not develop a hole in the deck. Run with: python scripts/validate_dimensions.py

tests.title: The parts manifest was built from the current control document
tests.rationale: You will edit GEOMETRY-CONTROL.md and forget to rebuild. This catches it every time.

tests.title: The generated geometry was built from the current control document
main_span + 2 x side_span_each equals bridge_proper_length
bridge_proper_length plus both approaches equals the stated total length
tests.rationale: Five independently lettered dimensions from SRC-002 sum to that drawing's own stated 5989 ft with zero residual. The strongest single check in the repository.

tests.title: The Manhattan approach gradient chain reaches the sourced anchorage elevation
tests.rationale: Terminus elevation and gradient come from SRC-002; the anchorage roadway elevation comes from SRC-004, a different document by a different author 80 years apart. Both sides land about 2.5 ft low with the same sign, which reads as a systematic curb-line versus grade-line offset rather than an error in the chain.

tests.title: The Brooklyn approach gradient chain reaches the sourced anchorage elevation
tests.rationale: Same cross-check on the other side, and it also confirms where the 129 ft anchorage block sits in the dimension chain.

tests.title: The tower arch closes on its own sourced radius, width and height
tests.rationale: A two-centred arch of radius 46 ft spanning 33.75 ft rises 35.6 ft; SRC-002 annotates 36 ft. Three independently drawn numbers that did not have to agree.

tests.title: NYCDOT's 2016 promenade typology agrees with HAER's 1883 bridge length
tests.rationale: SRC-011's six on-structure typologies sum to 3378 ft against SRC-002's 3455.5 ft bridge proper length -- a residual of 77.5 ft, 2.2%. A 2016 pedestrian study by the city and a 1980s measured drawing of an 1883 structure, made for entirely unrelated purposes and neither derived from the other. The tolerance is 30 m, wide enough for the wood deck to start inside the anchorage faces and narrow enough to fail if a typology length were mistyped.

tests.title: The promenade's passage through a tower fits inside that tower
tests.rationale: SRC-011's 'Towers - 109 feet' is 54.5 ft per tower; SRC-002 dimensions the tower 59 ft thick along the bridge at mean high water. The promenade passage must fit inside the masonry, and it does -- by 4.5 ft, in the direction the taper predicts, since the promenade crosses the tower well above the waterline where the tower is narrower. Two sources a century apart, agreeing on something neither set out to measure.

tests.title: Count of parts whose provenance is MEASURED
tests.rationale: Expected to be zero until a survey or photogrammetry set is ingested. Computed, not hardcoded, so it changes honestly on the day one lands.

tests.title: Census of parts by provenance
No control's HO dimension rounds away to zero
tests.rationale: Below roughly 0.05 mm at 1:87.1 a dimension is a rendering detail rather than a scale component.

tests.title: No longitudinal gap anywhere in the deck chain
tests.rationale: The most expensive bug recorded in HOW-TO-DESIGN.md section 11: deck geometry stopping at the anchorage face, where the SUSPENDED structure ends, leaving the roadway terminating in mid-air. SRC-004 states the anchorage top surface IS roadway. This test was written before the deck was.

tests.title: The deck chain spans the full sourced total length of the bridge
Every deck segment has positive length
No longitudinal gap anywhere in the promenade chain
tests.rationale: The same defect as GRT-030, one level up. The walkway is the part a visitor actually stands on, and a hole in it is a hole in the thing being modelled.

tests.title: The promenade runs past the roadway terminus by the sourced Brooklyn Curve length
tests.rationale: This model's first build ended the walkway at Adams Street with the road. That is wrong: SRC-011 names a 910 ft Brooklyn Curve beyond it, SRC-012 puts its far end at Tillary and Boerum, and SRC-014 describes walking it. The defect also left the tourist staircase to DUMBO attached to nothing. The test asserts the overhang equals the sourced curve length, so deleting the curve or truncating it both fail.

tests.title: Promenade segments abut rather than overlap
tests.rationale: Continuity alone cannot catch this: an overlap has no gap, so GRT-033 passes while two slabs share the same space. The first build of this chain put each tower balcony inside its side span, at both ends, and every continuity test still reported clean.

tests.title: Deck segments abut rather than overlap
Every part matches a material rule
tests.rationale: The material table has no default. An unmatched part is a build failure, not a silent grey.

tests.title: No structural part falls through to the catch-all material rule
Placeholder count has not regressed
tests.rationale: Milestone 1 baseline. Raising this limit requires editing the number AND writing the argument for it here.

tests.title: Sourced control count has not regressed
Part count has not regressed
Every tower stands on its own sourced foundation depth
tests.rationale: The two caissons are 34 ft apart in depth. Averaging them would be invisible in a render and wrong in the record.

tests.title: Tower tops sit at the active tower height control, not the recorded HAER figure
tests.rationale: CONF-001. CTL-021 (276.6 ft) is recorded but must not reach the geometry.

tests.title: The canonical scene frame is a byte-for-byte copy of the shared contract
tests.rationale: HOW-TO-DESIGN.md section 12: copy the canonical frame byte-for-byte and verify by hash. Do not re-serialise it, and do not edit the anchor. The same bytes are carried by digital-3d-shared-contracts, manhattan-bridge-3d and dumbo-district-3d; a re-serialised copy would drift silently and only surface as a placement disagreement much later.

tests.title: No dimension callout is attached to a part whose provenance is ASSUMED
tests.rationale: If we do not know where it is, we do not get to say how big it is.
